<small>Source: Defra Strategic Architecture Principles, owned by the Strategic Architecture team. Changes to these principles are approved by the [Technology Governance Board](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/governance/tgb/).</small>

guardrails.title: Consider AI first
guardrails.statement: When designing a service or process, actively explore whether AI can improve quality, productivity, user experience or outcomes before choosing a traditional approach, and record the reasoning either way.
guardrails.evidence: ADR recording the AI options considered and why they were or were not used
guardrails.why: the DDTS doctrine says [assume AI until proven otherwise](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/principles/doctrine/#ddts-05). That does not mean AI everywhere; it means deliberately considering the opportunity before dismissing it.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
in discovery and alpha, look for repetitive tasks, triage, summarising, classification or decision support that AI could help with. Note in your ADR what you considered and why you did or did not use AI.

**In the AI digital toolkit:** start with [check if AI is right for your idea](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/triage/question-1), five questions about the problem, users, data, benefits and what you have tried.

guardrails.title: Use approved AI services and tenancies
guardrails.statement: Services you build run their AI in Defra's cloud tenancies or under approved enterprise agreements. When anyone uses an AI tool, they put Defra data into it only as the using data with AI rules in the AI digital toolkit allow - for example, never OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE or personal data in a public consumer tool.
guardrails.evidence: List of the AI services the service uses and the Defra tenancy or enterprise agreement each runs under

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Any AI services you are exploring identified, with the Defra tenancy or enterprise agreement they would run under
evidence_by_phase.alpha: AI services chosen for the design, each confirmed as running in a Defra tenancy or under an approved agreement
evidence_by_phase.beta: The AI services in the built service run only in approved tenancies, shown in the hosting design and configuration
evidence_by_phase.live: List of AI services in use, reviewed when services or agreements change

guardrails.title: Keep a human accountable
guardrails.statement: Decisions with legal or significant effects on people or organisations - such as licensing, enforcement or payments - have meaningful human oversight, and the ability to challenge.
guardrails.evidence: Design of the human oversight and challenge route, tested with users

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Design of the human oversight and challenge route for decisions with significant effects, tested with users in prototypes
evidence_by_phase.beta: Human review and challenge built into the service and tested with users and staff
evidence_by_phase.live: Records of human review, challenges raised and their outcomes, reviewed regularly

guardrails.title: Be transparent
guardrails.statement: Publish an Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard record for algorithmic tools that meet its scope, and tell users when they are interacting with AI.
guardrails.evidence: Link to the published Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard record and the AI notice shown to users

evidence_by_phase.beta: Draft Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard record, and the notice telling users about AI tested with them
evidence_by_phase.live: Link to the published Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard record, kept current

guardrails.title: Evaluate, monitor and threat model
guardrails.statement: Evaluate models for accuracy, bias and safety before release, monitor them in live, and include AI-specific threats (prompt injection, data leakage, model abuse) in your threat model.
guardrails.evidence: Model evaluation results for accuracy, bias and safety, live monitoring, and a threat model that covers AI-specific threats

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Evaluation plan for accuracy, bias and safety, and AI-specific threats in the threat model
evidence_by_phase.beta: Evaluation results for accuracy, bias and safety before release, and mitigations for AI threats tested
evidence_by_phase.live: Monitoring of model performance and drift in live, with evaluation repeated when the model or data changes

guardrails.title: Talk to the TDA about novel use
guardrails.statement: Novel uses of AI, and any use of generative AI in decision making, are reviewed by the Technical Design Authority.
guardrails.evidence: Technical Design Authority review outcome recorded in the ADR

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Novel or generative AI use in decision making identified, and a conversation with the Technical Design Authority booked
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Technical Design Authority review outcome recorded in the ADR
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Technical Design Authority review of any new AI use introduced by the change

guardrails.title: Suppliers use AI coding assistants openly and safely
guardrails.statement: Delivery partners who use AI coding assistants on Defra work agree which tools they use with Defra, use them only under terms that meet GR-AI-02, have a person review every change before it is merged, and say in pull requests or delivery reports where AI did significant work.
guardrails.evidence: Supplier's agreed list of AI coding assistants and how each runs within Defra-approved terms, the review process for generated code, and disclosure in pull requests or delivery reports
guardrails.why: AI coding assistants can speed up delivery, but they can also leak code, secrets or data to a third party, bring in code with unclear licences, and produce plausible but wrong code. Defra owns the code it pays for and must be able to trust it.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
- Follow [choosing a tool](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/choosing-a-tool) and [using data with AI](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/using-data-with-ai) in the AI digital toolkit: what matters is the data you put in, and privacy settings must be on.
- Tell the Defra engagement lead which tools you use at [mobilisation](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/partners/mobilisation/), and record them in the repository.
- Follow [AI security](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/security) in the AI digital toolkit: AI-written code clears the same Defra security gates as any other code.
- Never put secrets into prompts.
- Review AI-generated code with the same care as any other code ([GR-DEV-03](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/software-development/#gr-dev-03)), including licences of any suggested code.

This guardrail is a **draft** proposal. Comment on it by [opening an issue](https://github.com/DEFRA/architecture/issues).

guardrails.title: Give agents the least privilege they need
guardrails.statement: AI agents act under their own identity, with access only to the tools, data and actions their task needs, and never with a person's full permissions.
guardrails.evidence: List of each agent's tools and permissions, granted to the agent's own identity and reviewed

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Each agent's tools and permissions listed in the design, with a workload identity for the agent
evidence_by_phase.beta: Agent permissions configured as designed and tested, including that the agent cannot reach tools it should not
evidence_by_phase.live: Agent permissions reviewed regularly, as for a privileged user

guardrails.why: an agent can be tricked, or can be wrong. Limiting what it can reach limits the damage ([GR-IAM-03](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/identity-and-access/#gr-iam-03)).
guardrails.how_to_meet:
list each agent's tools and permissions, grant them to a workload identity for the agent, and review them as you would a privileged user's.

**In the AI digital toolkit:** [working with AI agents](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/working-with-agents).

guardrails.title: Get human approval for consequential actions
guardrails.statement: An agent does not take an action with legal, financial or significant effects on people, or one that cannot easily be undone, without approval from an accountable person.
guardrails.evidence: Design showing which agent actions need human approval, and tests proving they cannot happen without it

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Agent actions classified, and the actions that need human approval identified in the design
evidence_by_phase.beta: Approval enforced in the tool layer, with tests showing the agent cannot act without it
evidence_by_phase.live: Approval records reviewed, and the classification updated when the agent gains new tools

guardrails.why: [GR-AI-03](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/ai/#gr-ai-03) keeps a human accountable for decisions. Agents act faster than people can notice, so approval has to be designed in, not assumed.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
classify the agent's actions in alpha. Enforce approval in the tool layer, not only in the prompt, and test that the agent cannot bypass it.

**In the AI digital toolkit:** [working with AI agents](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/working-with-agents).

guardrails.title: Keep an audit trail of what agents do
guardrails.statement: Record what each agent was asked, what it read, which tools it called with what inputs, who approved what, and the outcome - and send security-relevant events to security monitoring.
guardrails.evidence: Audit records of agent inputs, tool calls, approvals and outcomes, sent to security monitoring

evidence_by_phase.beta: Audit records of agent inputs, tool calls, approvals and outcomes produced and sent to security monitoring
evidence_by_phase.live: Audit records retained and reviewed, and used to investigate any problem

guardrails.why: without a full record, nobody can explain, challenge or reverse what an agent did.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
log at the tool layer with correlation ids ([GR-OPS-02](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/observability-and-operations/#gr-ops-02)), and keep records for as long as the decisions they support.

**In the AI digital toolkit:** [working with AI agents](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/working-with-agents).

guardrails.title: Defend agents against prompt injection
guardrails.statement: Treat everything an agent reads - documents, emails, web pages, tool results - as untrusted input that may try to change its instructions, and design controls that hold even if it does.
guardrails.evidence: Threat model covering prompt injection through every input the agent reads, with tested mitigations

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Threat model covering prompt injection through every input the agent reads
evidence_by_phase.beta: Prompt injection mitigations tested, including attempts to misuse tools and leak data
evidence_by_phase.live: Prompt injection defences re-tested when inputs, tools or models change

guardrails.why: prompt injection is the most common way to make an agent misuse its tools or leak data.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
include injection through every input in your [threat model](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/security/threat-modelling/) ([GR-AI-05](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/ai/#gr-ai-05)), separate untrusted content from instructions, restrict tools as in GR-AI-08 and require approval as in GR-AI-09.

**In the AI digital toolkit:** [working with AI agents](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/working-with-agents).

guardrails.title: API first
guardrails.statement: Design the API for a capability before (or with) the user interface, so other services and partners can use it.
guardrails.evidence: API specification written before or alongside the user interface

guardrails.title: Describe APIs with open specifications
guardrails.statement: Synchronous APIs are described with OpenAPI 3, and asynchronous/event interfaces with AsyncAPI, kept in the same repository as the code.
guardrails.evidence: OpenAPI 3 or AsyncAPI documents in the service repository that match the running API

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Draft OpenAPI 3 or AsyncAPI documents for the interfaces you are prototyping
evidence_by_phase.beta: OpenAPI 3 or AsyncAPI documents in the repository, checked in the pipeline against the running API
evidence_by_phase.live: Specifications kept in step with every released change

guardrails.automated_check: Guardrail check (tools/guardrail-check): OpenAPI 3 and AsyncAPI documents present and well formed
guardrails.why: Machine-readable contracts make APIs discoverable, testable and safe to change.

guardrails.title: Follow government API standards
guardrails.statement: Follow the API technical and data standards: RESTful resources, JSON, HTTPS only, consistent error formats and standard identifiers from the data standards.
guardrails.evidence: API design reviewed against the GDS API technical and data standards

guardrails.title: Version and deprecate deliberately
guardrails.statement: Breaking changes are versioned, consumers are told in advance, and old versions have a published retirement date.
guardrails.evidence: Published versioning policy, deprecation notices sent to consumers and retirement dates for old versions

evidence_by_phase.beta: Versioning approach published for each API and event
evidence_by_phase.live: Deprecation notices sent to consumers and retirement dates published for old versions
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Consumers told about breaking changes in advance, with a new version and a retirement date for the old one
evidence_by_phase.retire: Consumers told the retirement date in advance, and moved to a replacement

guardrails.title: No integration through shared databases
guardrails.statement: Services do not read or write another service's database directly. Integrate through APIs, events or governed data products.
guardrails.evidence: Container diagram showing integration only through APIs, events or governed data products

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Container diagram showing integration only through APIs, events or governed data products
evidence_by_phase.beta: Built integrations match the container diagram, with no access to another service's database
evidence_by_phase.live: Integrations reviewed when the service or its dependencies change

guardrails.why: Shared databases tightly couple services and make both impossible to change safely.

guardrails.title: Use events for change notifications
guardrails.statement: Use asynchronous messages or events when other services need to react to something that happened (an application submitted, a permit issued), rather than polling.
guardrails.evidence: Event and message definitions described in AsyncAPI

guardrails.title: Secure every API
guardrails.statement: All APIs authenticate callers (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect or mutual TLS), authorise every request, validate input and apply rate limiting. No API is "internal so it's safe".
guardrails.evidence: Authentication and authorisation design, rate limits and input validation, covered by security testing

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Authentication, authorisation, input validation and rate limiting designed for each API
evidence_by_phase.beta: These controls built and covered by security testing
evidence_by_phase.live: API access reviewed, and controls re-tested after significant change

guardrails.title: Make APIs discoverable
guardrails.statement: Register APIs in the platform API catalogue and, where they are useful beyond Defra, the government API catalogue.
guardrails.evidence: Entry in the platform API catalogue

guardrails.title: Look for something to reuse first
guardrails.statement: Before buying or building, check the technology capability catalogue and cross-government components for something that already meets the need.
guardrails.evidence: ADR listing the reuse options considered from the technology capability catalogue and cross-government components

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Existing Defra and cross-government options for the need identified from the technology capability catalogue
evidence_by_phase.alpha: ADR recording the reuse options considered and why they did or did not fit
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: ADR showing reuse options considered for any new component

guardrails.why: Duplicate capabilities multiply cost, security risk and support effort.
guardrails.how_to_meet: Record in your ADR which strategic options you considered and why they did or did not fit. If a strategic option is close but not quite right, talk to the owning platform team before building around it.

guardrails.title: Buy commodity, build differentiating
guardrails.statement: Buy or use SaaS for commodity needs (email, HR, finance, CRM, document management). Build only where the capability is specific to Defra's mission and no product fits without heavy customisation.
guardrails.evidence: Buy or build options appraisal in the ADR or business case
guardrails.why: Heavily customised products combine the cost of building with the constraints of buying.
guardrails.how_to_meet: If you are configuring more than you are using out of the box, stop and reconsider. Prefer configuration over customisation; avoid modifying vendor code.

guardrails.title: Plan your exit before you enter
guardrails.statement: Any new product, platform or significant supplier dependency has a documented exit plan covering data export in open formats, contract terms and an estimate of switching cost.
guardrails.evidence: Exit plan covering data export in open formats, contract terms and an estimate of switching cost

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Draft exit plan for each new product, platform or significant supplier
evidence_by_phase.beta: Exit plan agreed, with contracts giving Defra its data and the right to export it in open formats
evidence_by_phase.live: Exit plan reviewed at contract renewal, with switching cost estimated
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Exit plan updated for any new product or supplier
evidence_by_phase.retire: Exit plan carried out - data exported in open formats and contracts ended

guardrails.why: Lock-in is sometimes a sensible trade-off, but it must be a deliberate one.
guardrails.how_to_meet: Include an exit section in your ADR or business case. Make sure contracts give Defra ownership of its data and the right to export it.

guardrails.title: Assess SaaS before you adopt it
guardrails.statement: SaaS and third-party hosted products are assessed for security, data protection, data location, accessibility and integration before contract.
guardrails.evidence: Supplier security assessment, DPIA where personal data is involved, data location, accessibility and single sign-on confirmed before contract

evidence_by_phase.discovery: SaaS and third-party products under consideration listed, with the assessments they will need
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Security, data protection, data location, accessibility and single sign-on assessed before contract

guardrails.why: Supply chain risk is one of the biggest sources of security incidents in government.
guardrails.how_to_meet: Use the [Secure by Design](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/security/secure-by-design/) supplier assurance activities, complete a DPIA if personal data is involved and confirm the product supports single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID for staff ([GR-IAM-02](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/identity-and-access/#gr-iam-02)).

guardrails.title: Prefer open standards and portable technology
guardrails.statement: Choose products and components that use open standards and can be run on more than one provider.
guardrails.evidence: ADR noting the open standards used and how portable the choice is
guardrails.why: Portability keeps our options open and our commercial position strong.

guardrails.title: Get spend approval early
guardrails.statement: Spend that falls under the government digital and technology spend control is discussed with the architecture team before procurement starts.
guardrails.evidence: Record of the conversation with the architecture team before procurement started

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Architecture team consulted before any procurement under spend control starts
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Architecture team consulted before new procurement for the change

guardrails.why: Architecture questions raised at the end of a procurement are expensive to answer.

guardrails.title: Every data set has an owner
guardrails.statement: Each data set a service creates or holds has a named business owner (information asset owner) and is recorded in the information asset register.
guardrails.evidence: Information asset register entries with a named owner for each data set

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Each data set the service will create or hold identified, with a proposed information asset owner
evidence_by_phase.beta: Information asset register entries with a named owner for each data set
evidence_by_phase.live: Register entries and owners kept current
evidence_by_phase.retire: Information asset register updated to show what happened to each data set

guardrails.why: Data without an owner is not maintained, not trusted and not deleted when it should be.

guardrails.title: Use authoritative sources
guardrails.statement: Use the authoritative source for shared entities - customers, organisations, land parcels, holdings, locations, species - rather than creating local copies that drift. See Defra on a page.
guardrails.evidence: Data flow diagram naming the authoritative source for each shared entity, with refresh arrangements for any copies

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Shared entities the service needs identified, with their authoritative sources
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Data flow diagram naming the authoritative source for each shared entity, and how any copies are refreshed
evidence_by_phase.beta: The service reads from the authoritative sources as designed, tested with the source owners
evidence_by_phase.live: Copies and refresh arrangements reviewed when sources change

guardrails.how_to_meet: If you must cache or replicate, record the source, refresh frequency and how you handle changes.

guardrails.title: Use agreed data standards and identifiers
guardrails.statement: Use the data standards for dates, addresses, locations, identifiers and code lists, so data can be joined across services.
guardrails.evidence: Data model that uses the agreed data standards and identifiers

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Data model using the agreed data standards and identifiers
evidence_by_phase.beta: Data stored and exchanged using the agreed standards, checked in testing

guardrails.title: Collect once, share safely
guardrails.statement: Do not ask users for information Defra already holds. Share data between services through APIs or governed data products, with data sharing agreements where required.
guardrails.evidence: Journey design showing users are not asked for information Defra already holds, and data sharing agreements where required

guardrails.title: Describe your data
guardrails.statement: Publish metadata for data sets so they can be found and understood - UK GEMINI for geospatial data and DCAT for other data sets.
guardrails.evidence: Published metadata records in UK GEMINI or DCAT

guardrails.title: Protect personal data by design
guardrails.statement: Complete a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) before processing personal data, minimise what you collect, and apply retention and deletion automatically.
guardrails.evidence: Approved DPIA, and retention and deletion built into the service

evidence_by_phase.discovery: DPIA screening completed, showing whether personal data is involved
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Draft DPIA, with data minimisation and retention designed in
evidence_by_phase.beta: Approved DPIA, and retention and deletion built and tested
evidence_by_phase.live: DPIA reviewed when processing changes, and deletion running as designed
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: DPIA updated for any change in how personal data is processed
evidence_by_phase.retire: Personal data deleted or transferred lawfully, as set out in the DPIA

guardrails.why: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018; TCoP point 7.

guardrails.title: Open by default
guardrails.statement: Publish non-personal, non-sensitive data as open data under the Open Government Licence, through the Defra Data Services Platform or data.gov.uk.
guardrails.evidence: Link to the published open data and its licence

guardrails.title: Manage data quality
guardrails.statement: Define, measure and report data quality using the Government Data Quality Framework, especially for data that feeds payments, regulatory decisions or official statistics.
guardrails.evidence: Data quality measures and regular reports

guardrails.title: Retain and dispose of records properly
guardrails.statement: Apply Defra's retention schedules. Records of permanent value are identified for transfer to The National Archives.
guardrails.evidence: Retention schedule applied and records of permanent value identified

evidence_by_phase.beta: Retention schedule identified for each type of record, and disposal built in
evidence_by_phase.live: Retention applied and records of permanent value identified for The National Archives
evidence_by_phase.retire: Records kept, transferred to The National Archives or destroyed, as agreed with the information asset owner

guardrails.title: Handle research data safely
guardrails.statement: Collect research data only with informed consent, store recordings and notes only in Defra-approved places, delete them when they are no longer needed, use only Defra-approved research tools, and screen research for a DPIA.
guardrails.evidence: Research plan showing consent, where recordings and notes are stored, when they are deleted, the approved tools used and DPIA screening

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Consent forms and privacy notice in use, recordings and notes stored only in approved places, and a deletion date set
evidence_by_phase.alpha: The same for alpha research, with DPIA screening done for the research and any new research tool assessed
evidence_by_phase.beta: Research data from earlier phases deleted on schedule, and the same controls for beta research
evidence_by_phase.live: Research data handled the same way for ongoing research, and deletion checked

guardrails.why: Research recordings and notes are personal data about real people. Keeping them in personal accounts, unapproved tools or for longer than needed puts participants at risk and breaks data protection law.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
- Get informed consent before each session, using the templates in the manual's [standards and guidance](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/user-research/standards-and-guidance).
- Store recordings and notes only where the manual's participant data storage and retention guidance says, and set a deletion date when you collect them.
- Use only the manual's [approved research tools](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/user-research/tools), and check a tool can hold the data you plan to collect. Assess any new tool before using it ([GR-TECH-04](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/choosing-technology/#gr-tech-04)).
- Screen the research for a DPIA ([GR-DATA-06](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/data/#gr-data-06)), especially for new tools, sensitive topics or recordings of people's homes or farms.
- Do not put recordings or transcripts into AI tools except as the [AI digital toolkit](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/ai-toolkit/guidance/keeping-data-safe) allows.

This guardrail is a **draft** proposal. Comment on it by [opening an issue](https://github.com/DEFRA/architecture/issues).

guardrails.title: No real personal data in prototypes
guardrails.statement: Prototypes, research materials and test environments use made-up or anonymised data, never real personal data copied from a live service or spreadsheet.
guardrails.evidence: Prototypes and test environments use made-up or anonymised data, never real personal data

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Prototypes and research materials use made-up data, including data a participant types in during a session
evidence_by_phase.beta: Test and research environments use synthetic or anonymised data; any exception agreed through a DPIA

guardrails.why: Prototypes are shared widely, hosted on less protected platforms and shown to participants. Real data in them can be seen by people who should not see it.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
make up realistic names, addresses, holdings and reference numbers. Tell participants not to enter their own real details into a prototype unless the research plan allows it and the data is handled under [GR-DATA-10](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/data/#gr-data-10). If a test genuinely needs real data, agree it through a DPIA first.

This guardrail is a **draft** proposal. Comment on it by [opening an issue](https://github.com/DEFRA/architecture/issues).

guardrails.title: Challenge paper and manual processes
guardrails.statement: Do not put a paper or email process online as it is. Find out why each step exists, and remove, automate or redesign it.
guardrails.evidence: Discovery findings showing paper, email and manual steps in the current process and how the new design removes or justifies each one
guardrails.why: digitising a broken process makes it faster to fail. The biggest gains come from removing steps, not speeding them up.
guardrails.how_to_meet: map the current process in discovery, including the parts staff do by hand. For each step, record whether it is needed, and why.

guardrails.title: Design across organisational boundaries
guardrails.statement: Design the end-to-end service from the user's point of view, even when parts of it are delivered by other Defra organisations or other parts of government.
guardrails.evidence: A map of the whole service, including the parts other teams and organisations deliver, and agreed hand-offs between them
guardrails.why: users do not care which organisation does what. Many Defra users deal with several Defra bodies for one task.
guardrails.how_to_meet: identify the whole service your work is part of, talk to the teams delivering the other parts, and agree how users and data move between them.

guardrails.title: Provide assisted digital and offline routes
guardrails.statement: Make sure people who cannot use the online service, or cannot use it alone, can still get what they need - with help, by phone or on paper - and that those routes lead to the same outcome and data.
guardrails.evidence: Assisted digital and offline routes designed and tested with users who need them
guardrails.why: some Defra users have limited internet access, skills or confidence, particularly in rural areas. Service Standard point 5 asks that everyone can use the service.
guardrails.how_to_meet: design assisted routes in alpha, so staff-assisted applications go through the same system as online ones rather than a separate process.

guardrails.title: Choose devices that suit the job
guardrails.statement: Choose devices for field work from research into where and how people work - outdoors, in bad weather, wearing gloves, in the dark - not from what is already on the desk.
guardrails.evidence: User research on the working environment, and the device choice recorded in an ADR
guardrails.why: a tool that cannot be used in the rain or with gloves on will not be used, and staff fall back to paper.
guardrails.how_to_meet: observe field work in discovery, and record the device choice and the reasons in an ADR.

guardrails.title: Design field tools to work offline
guardrails.statement: Field tools work without a connection: they download what is needed before a visit, save work on the device, and sync safely when back in signal.
guardrails.evidence: Field journeys tested with no connection, including sync after reconnecting and conflict handling
guardrails.why: much of rural England and the sea has poor or no mobile coverage. Losing work because the signal dropped destroys trust in digital tools.
guardrails.how_to_meet: test every field journey in flight mode, and decide in an ADR how conflicts are resolved when two people change the same record offline.

guardrails.title: Manage and secure every device
guardrails.statement: Devices that hold or access Defra data are enrolled in Defra device management, encrypted, kept patched, protected by a screen lock and able to be wiped remotely if lost.
guardrails.evidence: Devices enrolled in Defra device management, with encryption, patching and remote wipe confirmed

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Device management approach agreed for the devices the service will use
evidence_by_phase.beta: Devices enrolled in Defra device management, with encryption, patching, screen lock and remote wipe confirmed
evidence_by_phase.live: Device compliance monitored, and lost devices wiped

guardrails.why: field devices are lost and stolen more often than office equipment, and may hold personal and sensitive data.
guardrails.how_to_meet: use Defra-managed devices. If a supplier or partner device is needed, agree how it meets the same controls before it is used.

guardrails.title: Check connectivity before you design
guardrails.statement: Check the mobile and broadband coverage where the service will be used before choosing an approach, rather than assuming it.
guardrails.evidence: Connectivity in the places the service will be used checked, and the approach recorded
guardrails.why: coverage maps and real-world signal often differ, especially inside farm buildings and in valleys.
guardrails.how_to_meet: use public coverage data and ask users, and plan for the worst case.

guardrails.title: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA
guardrails.statement: Public and staff-facing services meet WCAG 2.2 level AA, are tested with assistive technology and publish an accessibility statement.
guardrails.evidence: Accessibility audit, assistive technology testing results and a published accessibility statement

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Prototypes built with accessible components, and a plan for an accessibility audit and assistive technology testing
evidence_by_phase.beta: Accessibility audit and assistive technology testing completed, issues fixed, and an accessibility statement published
evidence_by_phase.live: Accessibility statement kept current, and accessibility re-tested after significant change

guardrails.automated_check: Automated accessibility tests such as axe in the pipeline. These find some issues only; manual testing is still needed.
guardrails.why: It is the law (Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018) and Service Standard point 5.
guardrails.service_manual: [make sure everyone can use the service](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/accessibility), including the assistive technologies Defra staff use and when exemptions apply, [manage accessibility in your project](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/accessibility/manage-accessibility) and [test for accessibility](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/accessibility/test-for-accessibility).

guardrails.title: Use the GOV.UK Design System
guardrails.statement: Public-facing services use GOV.UK Frontend and patterns. Staff-facing services should use them too.
guardrails.evidence: The service uses GOV.UK Frontend and design decisions record where it departs from the patterns

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Prototypes built with the GOV.UK Design System, with departures recorded and researched
evidence_by_phase.beta: The service uses GOV.UK Frontend, with design decisions recording any departures
evidence_by_phase.live: GOV.UK Frontend kept up to date

guardrails.title: Progressive enhancement
guardrails.statement: Core journeys work without JavaScript, and are server-rendered. Use JavaScript to enhance, not to make things work.
guardrails.evidence: Core journeys tested with JavaScript turned off

guardrails.title: Consider forms platforms first
guardrails.statement: For form-based services, consider the forms options under Customer Service before building a bespoke front end.
guardrails.evidence: ADR noting whether the forms capability was considered

guardrails.title: Design for low bandwidth and rural users
guardrails.statement: Many Defra users - farmers, land managers, field staff - work in places with poor connectivity. Keep pages light, support saving progress, and consider offline working for field tools.
guardrails.evidence: Page weight budget, save-progress design and testing on slow connections

guardrails.title: Support Welsh where required
guardrails.statement: Services used in Wales meet the Welsh Language Standards where they apply. Design for translation from the start.
guardrails.evidence: Assessment of whether the Welsh Language Standards apply and translated content where they do

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Whether the Welsh Language Standards apply decided, and the service designed for translation
evidence_by_phase.beta: Welsh content and journeys built and tested where the standards apply
evidence_by_phase.live: Welsh content kept in step with English content

guardrails.title: Tell users what is happening when things fail or are slow
guardrails.statement: When a service is slow, a dependency fails or something is still being processed, users see a clear message saying what has happened, whether their work is saved, and what to do next - not a generic error or a page that seems to hang.
guardrails.evidence: Designed and tested content for each way the service can fail or slow down, and the front end showing it

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Each dependency that can fail or be slow identified with the developers, and what users see in each case designed and tested in the prototype
evidence_by_phase.beta: The front end shows the designed content when a dependency fails or is slow, tested by switching dependencies off
evidence_by_phase.live: Failure and delay content kept accurate as dependencies and processing times change

guardrails.why: Defra services depend on platforms and back-office systems that will sometimes be slow or unavailable. Users who are not told what is happening give up, try again and create duplicates, or phone for help.
guardrails.how_to_meet:
- With the developers, list each dependency that can fail or be slow, and decide what users see for each. This is the user-facing side of [GR-OPS-04](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/observability-and-operations/#gr-ops-04), which designs the service to degrade gracefully.
- Use the GOV.UK Design System [problem with the service pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/problem-with-the-service-pages/) and [service unavailable pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/service-unavailable-pages/), and say whether the user's answers are saved.
- For work that is processed later, show a status and a realistic time, as in the [asynchronous submission](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/patterns/async-submission/#content-to-design) pattern.
- Test these messages with users in alpha, and test the real failures in beta by switching dependencies off.

This guardrail is a **draft** proposal. Comment on it by [opening an issue](https://github.com/DEFRA/architecture/issues).

guardrails.title: Use Defra's strategic delivery platform by default
guardrails.statement: New digital services are hosted on the Defra Core Delivery Platform (CDP) unless an exception has been agreed.
guardrails.evidence: The service runs on the Core Delivery Platform, or an approved exception

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Platform team engaged, and any hosting needs the Core Delivery Platform might not meet identified
evidence_by_phase.alpha: The design runs on the Core Delivery Platform, or an exception has been requested
evidence_by_phase.beta: The service runs on the Core Delivery Platform, or under an approved exception
evidence_by_phase.live: The service still runs on the platform, and any exception is reviewed before it expires

guardrails.why: CDP provides secure-by-default hosting, CI/CD, observability, secrets management and protective monitoring once, for everyone. Each team that builds its own platform recreates this at its own cost and risk.
guardrails.how_to_meet: In discovery or alpha, work with the Delivery Architecture team to decide whether CDP is right for your service - the expectation is that it will be - and engage the platform team. If CDP cannot meet a requirement (for example specialist compute, a SaaS product or a legacy migration), raise an [exception](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/governance/exceptions/) early and tell the platform team - the gap may be something they should solve for everyone.
guardrails.service_manual: [Core Delivery Platform](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/architecture-and-software-development/core-delivery-platform). The manual says a service not on CDP is managed as an exception through the Delivery Architecture team's governance process; how that relates to exceptions on this site is [still being agreed](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/governance/exceptions/#exceptions-to-the-software-development-standards).

guardrails.title: Public cloud first
guardrails.statement: Where a service cannot use a strategic platform, it is hosted in a Defra-managed public cloud tenancy. New on-premises hosting is not permitted.
guardrails.evidence: Hosting design showing a Defra-managed public cloud tenancy

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Where the platform cannot be used, the hosting design uses a Defra-managed public cloud tenancy
evidence_by_phase.beta: The service runs in a Defra-managed public cloud tenancy
evidence_by_phase.live: No on-premises hosting introduced

guardrails.why: Government [Cloud First policy](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/government-cloud-first-policy) and Defra's data centre exit.

guardrails.title: Everything as code
guardrails.statement: Infrastructure, configuration, pipelines and policies are defined as code, version-controlled and deployed through automated pipelines. No manual changes to production.
guardrails.evidence: Infrastructure, configuration and pipeline code in the repository, and drift detection results

evidence_by_phase.beta: Infrastructure, configuration and pipelines defined as code in the repository, with no manual changes to production
evidence_by_phase.live: Drift detection running, and no manual changes to production in the change history

guardrails.why: Repeatable, reviewable, recoverable environments. Manual changes cause drift and incidents.
guardrails.how_to_meet: Use the platform's provided templates. Where you manage your own infrastructure, use a declarative tool such as Terraform and run drift detection.

guardrails.title: Use managed services before self-managed
guardrails.statement: Prefer managed cloud services (databases, queues, storage) over running your own on virtual machines.
guardrails.evidence: Hosting design listing the managed services used
guardrails.why: Managed services remove patching and much operational toil.

guardrails.title: Consistent, disposable environments
guardrails.statement: Have at least development, test and production environments, created from the same code, with production data never copied to lower environments unless anonymised.
guardrails.evidence: Environments created from the same code, and how lower environments avoid real personal data

guardrails.title: Host data in the UK
guardrails.statement: Data classified OFFICIAL is held in UK regions unless an assessed and approved exception exists.
guardrails.evidence: Data location confirmed for every data store and backup

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Hosting design places every data store and backup in UK regions
evidence_by_phase.beta: Data location confirmed for every data store and backup as built
evidence_by_phase.live: Data location checked when new stores or services are added

guardrails.why: Data protection, sovereignty and Defra's information risk appetite.

guardrails.title: Design for the resilience the service needs
guardrails.statement: Agree recovery time and recovery point objectives with the service owner, design to them across availability zones, and test recovery at least once a year.
guardrails.evidence: Agreed recovery time and recovery point objectives, a multi-zone design and the date of the last recovery test

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Recovery time and recovery point objectives agreed with the service owner, and a design that meets them
evidence_by_phase.beta: Multi-zone design built, and recovery tested before go-live
evidence_by_phase.live: Recovery tested at least once a year, with the date of the last test
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Recovery objectives and design checked for the change

guardrails.why: Some Defra services, such as flood warnings and disease control, are critical during emergencies - exactly when infrastructure is under stress.

guardrails.title: Use the strategic customer identity services
guardrails.statement: Services for citizens, farmers and businesses use Defra Customer Identity (Defra ID), which uses GOV.UK One Login and Government Gateway as identity providers, for authentication. Services do not build their own sign-in. See Defra Customer Identity in the Defra Digital Service Manual.
guardrails.evidence: Integration with Defra Customer Identity and the agreed level of identity assurance

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Identity team engaged about the level of identity assurance needed and how users act for organisations
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Sign-in designed with Defra Customer Identity, and tested with users
evidence_by_phase.beta: Integration with Defra Customer Identity built and tested
evidence_by_phase.live: No other sign-in introduced

guardrails.why: Users get one account across Defra services, we manage relationships between people and organisations (including agents) once, and we avoid storing credentials.
guardrails.how_to_meet: Talk to the Customer Identity team in discovery about the level of identity assurance you need and how the service will represent organisations and agents.

guardrails.title: Staff sign in with Microsoft Entra ID
guardrails.statement: Staff-facing services and products, including SaaS, use single sign-on through Microsoft Entra ID with multi-factor authentication. No local staff accounts.
guardrails.evidence: Single sign-on through Microsoft Entra ID with multi-factor authentication and no local staff accounts

evidence_by_phase.beta: Staff sign in through Microsoft Entra ID with multi-factor authentication, and there are no local staff accounts
evidence_by_phase.live: Staff access reviewed regularly through Entra ID groups

guardrails.why: Joiners, movers and leavers are handled in one place, and conditional access protects every product.

guardrails.title: Authorise on least privilege
guardrails.statement: Users, services and pipelines get only the permissions they need, granted through roles or groups, and reviewed regularly.
guardrails.evidence: Role and group model and a record of access reviews

evidence_by_phase.beta: Role and group model built, with users, services and pipelines given only the permissions they need
evidence_by_phase.live: Record of regular access reviews
evidence_by_phase.retire: All access to the service's systems and data removed

guardrails.title: Separate authentication from authorisation
guardrails.statement: Use the identity provider to establish who someone is; keep business authorisation rules (for example "can act for this holding") explicit, testable and in the right service.
guardrails.evidence: Authorisation rules written down and covered by automated tests

guardrails.title: No secrets in code
guardrails.statement: Secrets, keys and credentials are held in a managed secrets store, rotated, and never committed to source control. Use workload identity in preference to long-lived keys.
guardrails.evidence: Secrets held in a managed store with rotation and secret scanning enabled

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Secret scanning on from the first commit, and secrets held in a managed store from the start
evidence_by_phase.beta: All secrets in a managed store with rotation, using workload identity where possible
evidence_by_phase.live: Secrets rotated, and secret scanning alerts dealt with

guardrails.automated_check: GitHub secret scanning with push protection
guardrails.how_to_meet: Enable secret scanning on every repository ([GR-OPEN-03](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/open-source/#gr-open-03)).

guardrails.title: Privileged access is controlled and audited
guardrails.statement: Production and administrative access is just-in-time, uses phishing-resistant MFA, and is logged to the security operations centre.
guardrails.evidence: Just-in-time privileged access with phishing-resistant MFA and logs reaching the security operations centre

evidence_by_phase.beta: Just-in-time privileged access with phishing-resistant MFA configured, and logged to the security operations centre
evidence_by_phase.live: Privileged access reviewed regularly

guardrails.title: Use the platform's observability tooling
guardrails.statement: Send structured logs, metrics and traces to the platform's observability tooling, and security events to the security operations centre.
guardrails.evidence: Dashboards and alerts in the platform's observability tooling and security events reaching the security operations centre

evidence_by_phase.beta: Logs, metrics and traces reaching the platform's observability tooling, and security events reaching the security operations centre
evidence_by_phase.live: Dashboards and alerts in use by the team that runs the service

guardrails.title: Log in a structured, safe way
guardrails.statement: Use structured (JSON) logs with correlation identifiers across service boundaries. Never log secrets, tokens or unnecessary personal data.
guardrails.evidence: Sample logs showing structured fields and correlation identifiers and no secrets

evidence_by_phase.beta: Structured logs with correlation identifiers, tested to show no secrets or unnecessary personal data are logged
evidence_by_phase.live: Logging reviewed when new data or features are added

guardrails.title: Define and measure service levels
guardrails.statement: Agree service level objectives for availability, latency and correctness with the service owner, monitor them, and alert on what matters to users rather than on every metric.
guardrails.evidence: Agreed service level objectives with monitoring and alerts

guardrails.title: Health checks and graceful degradation
guardrails.statement: Expose health endpoints, set timeouts and retries on dependencies, and degrade gracefully (for example save progress and tell the user) when a dependency fails.
guardrails.evidence: Health endpoints, timeout and retry settings, and a design for when dependencies fail

guardrails.title: Be ready for live before you go live
guardrails.statement: Before public beta, agree the support model, on-call arrangements, runbooks, incident process and who owns the service in live. Register the service in the service catalogue.
guardrails.evidence: Support model, on-call arrangements, runbooks, incident process, named live owner and service catalogue entry

evidence_by_phase.beta: Before public beta, the support model, on-call arrangements, runbooks, incident process and live owner agreed, and the service catalogue entry made
evidence_by_phase.live: Runbooks and support arrangements tested and kept current
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Runbooks and support arrangements updated before the change goes live

guardrails.title: Learn from incidents
guardrails.statement: Hold blameless post-incident reviews for significant incidents and share the lessons in the open where appropriate.
guardrails.evidence: Post-incident reviews and the actions taken

guardrails.title: Measure performance and cost
guardrails.statement: Publish the mandatory key performance indicators and tag cloud resources so cost can be attributed to the service and business capability.
guardrails.evidence: Published key performance indicators and cost tags on cloud resources

guardrails.title: Code in the open
guardrails.statement: New source code is public from the start, in a Defra GitHub organisation, unless there is a recorded reason to keep a specific repository private (for example fraud rules or unannounced policy).
guardrails.area: Open source and working in the open
guardrails.evidence: Public repository in a Defra GitHub organisation, or a recorded reason for keeping it private

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Code public in a Defra GitHub organisation from the first commit, or a recorded reason for keeping a repository private
evidence_by_phase.beta: Repositories public, or the reasons for keeping them private reviewed
evidence_by_phase.live: Repositories still public, or private for a recorded reason
evidence_by_phase.retire: Repositories archived, not deleted, so the code and decisions stay available

guardrails.why: [Service Standard point 12](https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/service-standard/point-12-make-new-source-code-open). Openness also makes teams more careful about secrets and quality.

guardrails.title: Licence clearly
guardrails.statement: Code is released under the Open Government Licence or the MIT licence, with a LICENCE file in every repository.
guardrails.area: Open source and working in the open
guardrails.evidence: LICENCE file with the Open Government Licence or MIT licence in every repository

evidence_by_phase.alpha: LICENCE file in every repository from the start
evidence_by_phase.beta: LICENCE file with the Open Government Licence or MIT licence in every repository
evidence_by_phase.live: LICENCE file in every new repository

guardrails.automated_check: Guardrail check (tools/guardrail-check): LICENCE file with the Open Government Licence or MIT

guardrails.title: Publish safely
guardrails.statement: Enable secret scanning and push protection on every repository. Keep secrets, credentials and sensitive configuration out of code.
guardrails.area: Open source and working in the open
guardrails.evidence: Secret scanning and push protection enabled on every repository

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Secret scanning and push protection on for every repository from the first commit
evidence_by_phase.beta: Secret scanning and push protection on for every repository
evidence_by_phase.live: Secret scanning alerts dealt with promptly

guardrails.automated_check: Guardrail check (tools/guardrail-check): secret scanning and push protection turned on, with a token that can read security settings

guardrails.title: Reuse and contribute back
guardrails.statement: Use and improve existing open source and Defra components rather than forking or rewriting. Contribute fixes back upstream.
guardrails.area: Open source and working in the open
guardrails.evidence: Reuse and upstream contributions noted in ADRs and pull requests

guardrails.title: Blog and show the thing
guardrails.statement: Share what you learn on the Defra Digital blog, at show and tells, and in this repository.
guardrails.area: Open source and working in the open
guardrails.evidence: Blog posts, show and tells or contributions to this site

guardrails.title: Fund and run products, not projects
guardrails.statement: Build and run digital services as products, owned by a long-lived team that keeps improving them, rather than as projects that end at go-live.
guardrails.evidence: A named, long-lived team responsible for the product, with a roadmap beyond the current funding period
guardrails.why: services are used for years. When the team that built a service disbands at launch, knowledge is lost, technical debt grows and the service slowly fails its users.
guardrails.how_to_meet: plan funding and team continuity beyond go-live from the start. If a project model is unavoidable, agree before go-live which product team will own the service in live ([GR-OPS-05](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/guardrails/observability-and-operations/#gr-ops-05)).

guardrails.title: Name the product owner and service owner
guardrails.statement: Every product has a named product owner, and every service a named service owner, who are accountable for it throughout its life.
guardrails.evidence: Named product owner and service owner, recorded in the service catalogue
guardrails.why: decisions about priorities, risk and retirement need someone with the authority to make them.
guardrails.how_to_meet: record both in the service catalogue and in the repository README, and keep them current when people move on.

guardrails.title: Contribute to platforms rather than working around them
guardrails.statement: When a shared platform does not meet a need, raise it with the platform team and contribute to fixing it, rather than building a local workaround.
guardrails.evidence: Requests and contributions raised with platform teams, and ADRs where the team worked around a platform
guardrails.why: every workaround becomes something else to secure, support and eventually remove, and other teams have the same need.
guardrails.how_to_meet: talk to the platform team first. If you must work around a gap to meet a deadline, record it in an ADR with a plan to move back on to the platform.

guardrails.title: Plan for the end of a product's life
guardrails.statement: Know where each product is in its lifecycle - growing, stable, being replaced or retiring - and plan its retirement as deliberately as its launch.
guardrails.evidence: Product lifecycle stage recorded, with a retirement plan for products being replaced
guardrails.why: products that linger after they are replaced keep costing money and carrying risk.
guardrails.how_to_meet: record the lifecycle stage in the service catalogue, and follow [retire a service](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/deliver/retire/) when the time comes.

guardrails.title: Follow Secure by Design
guardrails.statement: Every new service and significant change follows the Secure by Design activities, with a named risk owner, from discovery onward.
guardrails.evidence: Named risk owner and the Secure by Design activities completed for the phase

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Named risk owner, and the information and threats the service is likely to face identified
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Secure by Design activities for alpha completed, including security requirements in the backlog
evidence_by_phase.beta: Secure by Design activities for beta completed, including controls built and tested
evidence_by_phase.live: Secure by Design activities for live continuing, including monitoring and review
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Secure by Design activities repeated for the change, with the risk owner involved

guardrails.how_to_meet: start from the patterns and checklists in the [Secure by Design artefact library](https://github.com/co-cddo/SbD) rather than designing controls from scratch.

guardrails.title: Keep a current threat model
guardrails.statement: Each service has a threat model, created by the team in alpha and revisited at every significant change and at least annually.
guardrails.evidence: Current, dated threat model, reviewed at the last significant change and at least annually

evidence_by_phase.alpha: First threat model, created by the team
evidence_by_phase.beta: Threat model updated as controls are built and tested
evidence_by_phase.live: Threat model reviewed at least once a year, with the date of the last review
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: Threat model revisited for the change before it is built

guardrails.title: Classify information
guardrails.statement: Identify the government security classification and data types the service handles, and design controls to match.
guardrails.evidence: Security classification and data types recorded with the controls that match them

evidence_by_phase.discovery: Security classification and the types of data the service will handle identified
evidence_by_phase.alpha: Controls in the design that match the classification

guardrails.title: Encrypt in transit and at rest
guardrails.statement: Use TLS 1.2 or higher for all traffic, internal and external, and encrypt data at rest using platform-managed or customer-managed keys.
guardrails.evidence: TLS configuration and encryption at rest settings for every data store

evidence_by_phase.beta: TLS 1.2 or higher for all traffic and encryption at rest for every data store, confirmed as built
evidence_by_phase.live: Encryption settings checked when new stores or connections are added

guardrails.title: Scan continuously and fix quickly
guardrails.statement: Run static analysis, dependency, container and infrastructure scanning in the pipeline. Fix critical vulnerabilities within 14 days and high within 30 days, or record a risk decision.
guardrails.evidence: Pipeline scanning results and the time taken to fix critical and high vulnerabilities

evidence_by_phase.beta: Static analysis, dependency, container and infrastructure scanning running in the pipeline
evidence_by_phase.live: Time taken to fix critical and high vulnerabilities, within 14 and 30 days, or a recorded risk decision

guardrails.automated_check: Static analysis, dependency, container and infrastructure scanning in the pipeline

guardrails.title: Test before go-live and after major change
guardrails.statement: Commission an independent IT health check (penetration test) proportionate to risk before go-live and after significant change, and track remediation.
guardrails.evidence: IT health check report and remediation tracker

evidence_by_phase.beta: IT health check before go-live, and a remediation tracker
evidence_by_phase.live: IT health check after significant change, with remediation tracked
evidence_by_phase.significant-change: IT health check scoped and booked for the change where it is significant

guardrails.title: Log for detection and response
guardrails.statement: Send security-relevant events (authentication, authorisation failures, administrative actions, data exports) to the security operations centre. See GR-OPS-01.
guardrails.evidence: Security-relevant events reaching the security operations centre

evidence_by_phase.beta: Authentication, authorisation failures, administrative actions and data exports sent to the security operations centre, and tested
evidence_by_phase.live: Security events reviewed and alerts acted on

guardrails.title: Protect the supply chain
guardrails.statement: Assess suppliers and third-party products for security before use, pin and verify dependencies, and know what is in your software (keep a software bill of materials).
guardrails.evidence: Supplier security assessments, pinned dependencies and a software bill of materials

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Security assessment of suppliers and third-party products in the design
evidence_by_phase.beta: Dependencies pinned and verified, and a software bill of materials produced in the pipeline
evidence_by_phase.live: Software bill of materials kept current, and supplier assessments reviewed at renewal

guardrails.automated_check: Dependency review and software bill of materials generation in the pipeline

guardrails.title: Manage risk explicitly
guardrails.statement: Where a control cannot be met, record the risk and get it accepted by the right owner through the security exception process. Accepted risks are time-limited.
guardrails.evidence: Risk register entries with an owner and an expiry date for every accepted risk

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Risks from controls that cannot be met recorded, with an owner
evidence_by_phase.beta: Residual risks accepted by the right owner through the security exception process, each with an expiry date
evidence_by_phase.live: Accepted risks reviewed before they expire

guardrails.title: Use the supported languages and frameworks
guardrails.statement: Use Defra's approved technologies and languages for new services so that skills, libraries and support are shared.
guardrails.evidence: ADR recording the reason wherever the service uses a different stack
guardrails.why: A small, well-supported set of technologies makes it easier to move people between teams, share components and support services for the long term.
guardrails.how_to_meet: If you need something else, request it through the Tools Radar and record the reason in an ADR, including how the service will be supported after the team moves on. The Delivery Architecture team handles exceptions to the software development standards.

guardrails.title: All code in Defra source control
guardrails.statement: All source code, including infrastructure and pipeline code written by suppliers, lives in a Defra-owned GitHub organisation from day one.
guardrails.evidence: All source code in a Defra-owned GitHub organisation from the first commit

evidence_by_phase.alpha: All code, including prototypes and infrastructure code written by suppliers, in a Defra-owned GitHub organisation from the first commit
evidence_by_phase.beta: All source, infrastructure and pipeline code in the Defra GitHub organisation, with nothing held only by a supplier
evidence_by_phase.live: All changes made in the Defra GitHub organisation

guardrails.why: Defra owns what it pays for and must be able to change supplier without losing code or history.

guardrails.title: Protect the main branch
guardrails.statement: Main branches are protected: changes arrive through pull requests with at least one review and passing automated checks.
guardrails.evidence: Branch protection on the main branch requiring a review and passing checks

evidence_by_phase.alpha: Main branch protected from the start, with changes through reviewed pull requests
evidence_by_phase.beta: Branch protection requiring at least one review and passing checks
evidence_by_phase.live: Branch protection still in place on every repository

guardrails.automated_check: Guardrail check (tools/guardrail-check): default branch protected by branch protection or a ruleset

guardrails.title: Continuous integration and delivery
guardrails.statement: Every change is built, tested, scanned and deployed by an automated pipeline. Releases to production are small, frequent and reversible.
guardrails.evidence: Pipeline definition in the repository and deployment history

evidence_by_phase.beta: Every change built, tested, scanned and deployed by an automated pipeline, with rollback tested
evidence_by_phase.live: Deployment history showing small, frequent, reversible releases

guardrails.title: Automated testing at the right levels
guardrails.statement: Use a balanced set of automated tests - unit, integration/contract, end-to-end journey, accessibility, performance and security - run in the pipeline.
guardrails.evidence: Test results from the pipeline at each level

guardrails.title: Manage dependencies actively
guardrails.statement: Use automated dependency updates and software composition analysis, and keep runtimes on supported versions.
guardrails.evidence: Dependabot or Renovate configuration and runtimes on supported versions

evidence_by_phase.beta: Dependabot or Renovate configured, software composition analysis in the pipeline, and runtimes on supported versions
evidence_by_phase.live: Dependency updates merged promptly and runtimes upgraded before they go out of support

guardrails.automated_check: Guardrail check (tools/guardrail-check): Dependabot or Renovate configured
guardrails.why: Unpatched dependencies are one of the most common ways services are compromised.

guardrails.title: Follow shared coding standards
guardrails.statement: Use automated linting and formatting, and follow the Defra software development standards, so code looks and behaves consistently across teams.
guardrails.evidence: Linting and formatting checks in the pipeline
guardrails.automated_check: Lint and format checks in the pipeline

guardrails.title: Document as you go
guardrails.statement: Each repository has a README explaining what it does, how to run it locally, how to test it and how to deploy it, and links to its ADRs.
guardrails.evidence: README explaining what the service does and how to run, test and deploy it, with links to its ADRs
guardrails.automated_check: Guardrail check (tools/guardrail-check): README sections on running, testing and deploying, and a link to ADRs

guardrails.title: Record significant decisions as ADRs
guardrails.statement: Record significant architecture decisions as architecture decision records (ADRs), kept with the code or linked from the repository's README.
guardrails.evidence: ADR log in the repository or linked from its README
guardrails.why: the reasons behind a design are lost when people move on. ADRs let the next team, an assessor or a partner taking over the service understand what was decided and why, and change it safely.
guardrails.how_to_meet: keep ADRs in a `docs/adr` folder in the service repository, using the [ADR template](https://howellsr.github.io/architecture/governance/templates/adr/). Write one when you make a decision that is hard to reverse, departs from a guardrail, or that someone will later ask "why did we do this?".

guardrails.title: Consider sustainability in design decisions
guardrails.statement: Include environmental impact as a factor in ADRs for hosting, architecture and technology choices.
guardrails.evidence: Environmental impact recorded in ADRs for hosting and technology choices
guardrails.service_manual: [assess risks and record sustainability actions](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/sustainability/process) - record the decisions in your sustainability statement as well as your ADRs.

guardrails.title: Right-size and switch off
guardrails.statement: Use autoscaling, scale non-production environments down out of hours, and delete unused resources.
guardrails.evidence: Autoscaling and out-of-hours schedules for non-production environments

guardrails.title: Choose lower-carbon regions and services
guardrails.statement: Where data rules allow, prefer cloud regions and services with lower carbon intensity, and use providers' carbon reporting.
guardrails.evidence: Region and service choice recorded with its carbon intensity

guardrails.title: Keep data and pages lean
guardrails.statement: Store only the data you need, for as long as you need it, and keep page weight low - which also helps users on slow connections (GR-FE-05).
guardrails.evidence: Data retention settings and page weight measurements

guardrails.title: Measure and report
guardrails.statement: Track the carbon footprint of your service using cloud provider tooling and report it alongside cost.
guardrails.evidence: Carbon footprint reported alongside cost
guardrails.service_manual: the [metrics for each of Defra's six objectives](https://digital.defra.gov.uk/sustainability/metrics).
